programmes.d: Oscar winner Jimmy Stewart describes an evening at the celebrity-fave nightclub when teenager Judy Garland showed up and sang for the gang.
Two-time Oscar winner Elizabeth Taylor chats about, her new perfume, addiction programs, her seven husbands, and her most marriage to construction worker Larry Fortensky.
Screen star and two-time Tony winner Lauren Bacall talks about her new play, life in LA and quitting smoking...for the fifth time.
Hollywood's best bad guy, Jack Palance says he doesn't like playing villains but loved his role a psychotic antiques dealer in his latest movie, Craze.
Comedian, TV star and noted humanitarian Danny Thomas chats about working with fellow funny man Jonathan Winters and his latest show on NBC.
Fellow talk show host and chart-topping vocalist Dinah Shore sings 2 of her hits and says she'd rather be the one asking the questions. Her dream interview is Israeli Prime Minister Golda Meir.
Movie star Tony Curtis discusses his steamy new novel about Hollywood and the mob. Also shows a clip from his first movie, at age 23, in which he played a rumba dancer.
The ultimate Hollywood bad guy, Jack Palance chats with Johnny about his break-out role in Shane (1949). Palance also describes his current line of work -- running a cattle ranch.
Hollywood leading man Gregory Peck dishes on WW2 hero General Douglas MacArthur, whom he played in the biopic, and the General's overlooked sense of humor.

Remember The Thorn Birds? Meet Colleen McCullough, who wrote the blockbuster novel-turned-mini series. Lou Brock discusses his base-stealing record and acting legend Eli Wallach chats about his craft. Don Rickles plugs his show C.P.O. Sharkey.
Screen star Peter O'Toole was Oscar nom'd 8 times! Never won. Finally bagged the golden statue for lifetime achievement. O'Toole discusses The Stunt Man. Comic Buddy Hackett brings some laughs.
The gorgeous and talented Ann-Margret says she disguises herself in a black wig when out in public. Screen legend Robert Mitchem reveals he did time on a chain gang, at age 15.
Hollywood heavyweights Jack Lemmon and Walter Matthau regale Johnny with tales of making 5 movies together and one near-death stunt gone very wrong.
Stardom is bad for your health. Walter Matthau dons dark glasses to disguise an eye problem, jokes about his roommate in the hospital and the awful food.
Sean Connery gives a Bond trivia quiz, and recalls his scariest stunts. Comic Keenan Ivory Wayans says dating white girls is like being on Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom; people can't stop staring.
Mickey Rooney compares notes with Johnny on their many marriages. Comic Paul Rodriguez riffs on Mexicans picking fruit and the fun of annoying white drivers on LA freeways.
We're spelling tonight! Walter Matthau and Johnny quiz one another on difficult words. Matthau recalls filming Tunisia and shows a clip from his movie, Pirates.
Hog wild: That's Jay Leno who owns 17 motorcycles. Leno describes a chopper breakdown in LA with a busload of tourists cheering him on. Raquel Welch discusses her children and getting older.
Not your typical leading man, Dennis Hopper talks about his unusual roles in Blue Velvet and Easy Rider, and his up and down career which began in his Kansas hometown.
Mr. "make-my-day" Clint Eastwood reminisces about Gunsmoke, Outlaw Josey Wales and Dirty Harry, while Bob Hope and David Letterman also appear.
Activist and two-time Oscar winner Jane Fonda details her suit against the US government for invading her privacy. Also plugs her move, "Julia."
Star party guy, Dean Martin recounts the wild fun celebrating Frank Sinatra's big 6-0. Also fills in Johnny on playing Las Vegas and his frequent forays into the casinos.
Brat packer & longtime TV personality Joey Bishop talks about his career, politics, how he gave up smoking and lost weight.
